title: Vitrification of Mucosal Biopsies
author: Sean M. Hughes
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p6adrae
materials: The biopsy is ready for use.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Materials
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary media and aluminum foil pieces for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1X vitrification medium (20% ethylene glycol, 20% dimethylsulfoxide in saline with fetal bovine serum).
Prepare 0.5X vitrification medium (10% ethylene glycol, 10% dimethylsulfoxide in saline with fetal bovine serum).
Prepare thawing medium (10% ethylene glycol, 10% dimethylsulfoxide in culture medium of interest).
Cut rectangular aluminum foil pieces that are narrower than the width of a cryovial and shorter than the height of the cryovial (up to the cap threads), ensuring they fit easily into a cryovial.

steps.title: Set Up Vitrification Station
steps.instruction: Prepare the cooling and freezing environment.

substeps.instruction: Place 5 mL of 0.5X vitrification medium in one well of a six-well plate and 5 mL of 1X vitrification medium in a second well.
Refrigerate the six-well plate at 4°C for 30 minutes.

Prepare a pan of liquid nitrogen with absorbent cloth and a cryovial rack so the bottom of the vials are immersed; ensure a section of the pan has enough exposed liquid nitrogen to immerse biopsies at least one inch deep.
Place empty cryovials in the rack within the liquid nitrogen container to pre-cool them.

steps.title: Process Biopsies for Vitrification
steps.instruction: Prepare and equilibrate the mucosal biopsies.

substeps.instruction: Prepare biopsies to be 5mm x 5mm or smaller.
Remove the six-well plate from the refrigerator and place it in a biosafety cabinet.
Transfer biopsies with forceps into the 0.5X solution and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Transfer biopsies with forceps into the 1X solution and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Briefly blot biopsies individually on a Kimwipe or sterile wipe to remove excess vitrification medium.

steps.title: Vitrify and Store Biopsies
steps.instruction: Rapidly freeze the biopsies using the foil-plunge method.

substeps.instruction: Place a biopsy close to the edge at the narrow end of a pre-cut piece of aluminum foil.
Pick up the other end of the foil with forceps and plunge the entire foil (and some of the forceps) into liquid nitrogen.
After approximately 10 seconds (once bubbling subsides), place the foil with the frozen biopsy into a pre-cooled cryovial (typically 3-4 biopsies per vial).
Cap the cryovials and store in a liquid nitrogen freezer.

steps.title: Prepare Thawing Station
steps.instruction: Set up the media for the recovery process.

substeps.instruction: Place 5 mL of thawing medium in one well of a six-well plate and 5 mL of plain culture medium in a second well.
Keep the plate at room temperature.

steps.title: Thaw and Recover Biopsies
steps.instruction: Recover the biopsies from the frozen state.

substeps.instruction: Remove cryovials from the liquid nitrogen freezer, keeping them on liquid nitrogen in a pan or carrying device.
Unscrew the caps while keeping the vials on liquid nitrogen.
Use forceps to remove one piece of aluminum foil/biopsy from a cryovial.
Quickly move the foil out of the liquid nitrogen pan and place it biopsy-side down in the thawing medium; shake for approximately 5 seconds until the biopsy detaches.
Use forceps to transfer the biopsy to the culture medium.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes (repeated twice in original text).
